points.quote: This Policy is based on the position that the use of GenAI tools for assessments is acceptable provided such tools are used responsibly, and academic integrity is maintained.
points.gist: Using GenAI tools for assessments is acceptable as long as they are used responsibly and academic integrity is maintained.

points.quote: There may be assessment contexts where the use of GenAI tools is not appropriate, and module tutors should make this clear in assignment briefs.
points.gist: Some assessments may not allow GenAI, and module tutors should say so in assignment briefs.

points.quote: Within all modules, academic staff should clearly articulate the acceptable use of GenAI tools by students (or where in a specific context such use may not be appropriate), based on this Policy and associated guidance.
points.gist: Academic staff should clearly state, in every module, what GenAI use by students is acceptable or not appropriate.

points.quote: there should be clarity for students on how they should acknowledge and reference the use of GenAI (see Cite them right guidance here).
points.gist: Students should be given clarity on how to acknowledge and reference GenAI use, with Cite them right guidance referred to.

points.quote: The importance of students maintaining a record of how they planned and constructed their assignment, detailing the use of GenAI where appropriate, should be embedded as part of good academic practice.
points.gist: Students keeping a record of how they planned and built an assignment, including any GenAI use, should be embedded as good academic practice.

points.quote: Staff should note that tools designed to detect the use of GenAI are known to be problematic and therefore their use is not currently permitted by the University.
points.gist: GenAI detection tools are known to be problematic and the University does not currently permit their use.

points.quote: We are aware of the challenges for students in relation to the digital divide and therefore recommend the use of Microsoft Co-pilot in relation to academic work.
points.gist: Because of the digital divide, the University recommends using Microsoft Co-pilot for academic work.

points.quote: students might be encouraged to use GenAI tools to prepare for classes and seminars or workshops, and also in relation to aspects of assessment preparation.
points.gist: Students might be encouraged to use GenAI tools to prepare for classes, seminars and workshops and for aspects of assessment preparation.

points.quote: the University Library Services will maintain advice and guidance for students on webpages, including examples of what is and is not acceptable.
points.gist: Library Services will maintain webpages of student guidance, including examples of what is and is not acceptable.

points.quote: Students should be explicitly alerted to these policies whenever GenAI is to be used.
points.gist: Students should be explicitly alerted to the privacy policies or user agreements whenever GenAI is to be used.

points.quote: Where GenAI tools are used by academic staff to create course materials, this should be clearly articulated and referenced within the learning materials or assessments.
points.gist: Staff using GenAI to create course materials should clearly state and reference this within the materials or assessments.

points.quote: All academic staff have an individual responsibility to review their assessments to mitigate the effects of the inappropriate use of GenAI tools.
points.gist: Every academic member of staff is individually responsible for reviewing their assessments to reduce the effects of inappropriate GenAI use.

points.quote: Course and module handbooks should be updated to include details of the University’s policy regarding the use of GenAI tools by students and its implementation within the School.
points.gist: Course and module handbooks should include the University policy on student GenAI use and how the School implements it.

points.quote: our position is not to prohibit the use of GenAI tools, but rather to provide all members of the academic community with support and guidance on how GenAI can be used responsibly and ethically
points.gist: The University's position is not to prohibit GenAI tools but to give support and guidance on responsible, ethical use.
